RFC5625:
   Whilst TCP transport is not strictly mandatory, it is supported by
   the vast majority of stub resolvers and recursive servers.  Lack of
   support in the proxy prevents this fail-over mechanism from working.
DNS proxies MUST therefore be prepared to receive and forward queries
   over TCP.

chat.author: Ted Lemon
chat.text: @lorenzo to go back to your earlier question, the thing we don't want to have happen is for a SNAC-router-generated ULA prefix to be used by a host on the infrastructure network as a source address.

chat.author: Ted Lemon
chat.text: (that is, when sending a message to an arbitrary other ULA prefix). It's essentially going to be a last resort to use when there is no IPv4 and no other IPv6 source address.

chat.author: Philipp Tiesel
chat.text: @Lorenzo: I have different experience with Rule 1 with some applications that don't use getaddrinfo and implement something themselves … but consider that broken

chat.author: Tom Hill
chat.text: Hosts expect IPv4 to work, they should expect IPv6 to work too. If IPv6 isn't working, the network has done something wrong.

chat.author: Tom Hill
chat.text: I don't believe this would change the minds of Enterprise network operators (their objections to IPv6 connectivity are more fundamental than 'does it work')

chat.author: Philipp Tiesel

chat.author: Tom Hill
